why: The best unconditional growth exponent for zeta(1/2+it) remains Bourgain's 13/84 from 2016 (pre-snapshot, no post-2024 improvement found), but 2024/2026 papers (Hiary-Patel-Yang; Revers) give improved explicit constants for the classical t^(1/6) log t bound on |zeta(1/2+it)|; unclear whether an explicit-constant tightening on a bound about the same quantity counts as moving the problem per the deep-dive's finer judgment.
